rv.q: At a time when so many stage shows are based on films, it is odd that it has taken so long for Shakespeare in Love to arrive in the West End. But boy has it been worth the wait.

“Comedy, love – and a bit with a dog. That's what they want,” declares Thomas Henslowe, the debt-ridden theatre manager in Shakespeare in Love. We'll come to the love in a moment. But first things first.
I've often attacked our modern mania for turning movies into plays. But, in the case of Shakespeare in Love, the transformation is fully justified.
Like many such beverages, this show is moderately fizzy and leaves a slightly synthetic aftertaste.

Can an adaptation be too faithful? Directed with verve by Declan Donnellan across, up and down Nick Ormerod’s versatile Elizabethan theater set, the 28-strong cast of this grand screen-to-stage adaptation of Shakespeare in Love (backed by Disney Theatrical and Sonia Friedman Prods.) fills the stage with high-spirited comedy.

cn.t: Critics praise this joyous stage adaptation as an improvement over the Oscar-winning film, celebrating Lee Hall's witty script as a love letter to theatre itself. The production delivers high-spirited comedy with verve and genuine emotional warmth.
